source_refs.note: Topic 2.2.1.2 Variable Naming Rules (PDF 36, printed 33). MCQ 3 is answered (printed options 'variablel' and 'Ivariable' read as variable1 and 1variable).

blocks.text: Variable names in Python must adhere to the following rules:

items: The name must begin with a letter (a-z, A-Z) or an underscore ( _ ).
Subsequent characters can include letters, digits (0-9), or underscores ( _ ).
Variable names are case-sensitive, meaning age and Age are considered two different variables.
Python's reserved keywords, such as for, while, if, etc., cannot be used as variable names.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Always use meaningful names for variables to make your code easier to understand. For example, use age instead of a.
